title: Mitigating Noise-Induced Layout Priors for Object Counting in Diffusion Models
claim: Initial noise, not the prompt, largely fixes spatial layout and object count, and early attention maps reveal this layout prior.
layout: 3 panels: left image grid, right top attention heatmaps, right bottom pairs
description: The figure has three panels separated by dashed lines. Panel (a), on the left, is a 3x5 grid of generated photos. Columns are birds, zebras, sheep, horses and cups. Rows are the prompts 'three', 'four' and 'five'. All use the same seed (271828). Each column shows nearly identical layouts, with four objects in a row regardless of the requested number. Panel (b), top right, shows viridis-colored cross-attention heatmaps for the 'cups' token in 'A photo of four cups'. It covers two seeds across steps 3, 5, 10 and 50, plus the final image. Panel (c), bottom right, pairs early-stage (step 5) attention maps with bird images for 'three birds', 'four birds' and 'five birds' under a fixed noise. The attention maps look the same, and so does the layout. Bold serif captions sit under each panel. The eye goes first to the large photo grid.
caption: Initial noise strongly governs spatial layout and object count in text-to-image diffusion models. (a) With fixed initial noise,
abstract: Despite remarkable progress in text-to-image diffusion models, accurately generating the specified number of objects remains a persistent challenge. We identify the initial noise as a primary determinant of spatial layout formation, with early-stage cross-attention serving as the key mechanism that mediates the propagation of noise-induced structures throughout the denoising process. We characterize this phenomenon as \textbf{\textit{Noise-Induced Layout Prior}}. Leveraging this insight, we propose a novel training-free framework for object counting in diffusion models. Our approach consists of two key components: (1) a \emph{Count-Aware Noise Adjustment Strategy}, which explicitly manipulates the initial latent noise to align layout formation with the target object count, and (2) an \emph{Attention-Guided Layout Consistency Strategy}, which performs test-time optimization on early-stage cross-attention to further stabilize layout formation during denoising. Extensive experiments on both single-category and multi-category benchmarks demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms strong diffusion baselines and state-of-the-art object count control methods in terms of counting accuracy and image quality. Code Release: \url{https://github.com/lxlong1201/Mitigate Noise Prior}.
